destination.title: Gravitational EFTs: completion, validity and low-energy consequences
destination.question: How can proposed quantum-gravity completions, limits of gravitational EFTs and possible low-energy consequences be tested?
destination.summary: No original verbal region scope was supplied. The numerical membership is usable for broad navigation, but interpreting every source as a Swampland exclusion would conflate conditional conjectures, ordinary dynamical calculations and constructive approaches. This wording is a new scope proposal requiring independent review.

systems: Gravitational EFTs with varied matter sectors, spectra and dimensions
String compactifications and alternative proposed ultraviolet completions
targets: Gravitational cutoffs, towers and field-space limits
regimes: Weak gauge coupling, massive mediators, large dimension and gravity decoupling
Ordinary semiclassical calculations and proposed ultraviolet descriptions
assumptions: No conjecture is imposed across the family
Numerical proximity does not establish scientific equivalence
Each conditional calculation retains its own premises
conventions: Distinguish full theories from their lower-dimensional descriptions
Distinguish physical thresholds, perturbative cutoffs, species scales and quantum-gravity scales
Preserve supplied source dates and versions
includes: Boundary tests and useful alternative approaches
Open questions and speculative proposals with their status visible
excludes: A universal classification of quantum-gravity completions
Guaranteed solutions to naturalness or cosmological problems
Promotion of extracted graph relations into family-wide physical premises

sources.title: Black Holes and Large N Species Solution to the Hierarchy Problem

evidence.text: Can a large number of quantum-field species force gravity to be weak relative to their mass scale, thereby explaining the weak–Planck hierarchy and the Higgs mass's sensitivity to a much larger cutoff?

sources.title: Gravity Cutoff in Theories with Large Discrete Symmetries

evidence.text: Does an exact quantum number of large periodicity N require a gravitational cutoff below MP even without N particle species, and under what assumptions could this protect the weak scale?

sources.title: Axion Experiments to Algebraic Geometry: Testing Quantum Gravity via the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Can a stronger, lattice-wide weak-gravity requirement characterize consistent quantum gravity and yield testable constraints on axions, conformal field theories, and compactification geometry?

sources.title: Constraining Neutrino Masses, the Cosmological Constant and BSM Physics from the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Can consistency with quantum gravity restrict the infrared particle spectrum and vacuum energy through the absence of stable AdS solutions of compactified effective theories?

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Remnants from the String Landscape

evidence.text: Can characteristic low-energy remnants or violations of established quantum-gravity restrictions test a theory with an inaccessible fundamental scale and many possible vacua?

sources.title: Emergence of Weak Coupling at Large Distance in Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Can infrared properties of scalar fields and particle towers identify gravitational EFTs compatible with quantum gravity? A separate unresolved issue is whether quantum gravity itself guarantees moduli and towers becoming massless in large-moduli limits.

sources.title: Theta-problem and the String Swampland

evidence.text: Could quantum-gravity consistency select the observed QCD or QED theta angle and impose an arithmetic condition on the physical electromagnetic coupling?

sources.title: A Spin‐2 Conjecture on the Swampland

evidence.text: The paper asks whether quantum gravity imposes a tower threshold on a fundamental massive spin-2 field, beyond the requirements of infrared consistency. The associated massless limit would otherwise produce an additional massless spin-2 field.

sources.title: Modular symmetries and the swampland conjectures

evidence.text: What restrictions should quantum gravity impose on infinite-distance limits and positive scalar potentials?

sources.title: Swampland, Gradient Flow and Infinite Distance

evidence.text: Does a large-radius limit require new states in the full theory, or does it reveal states already present when that theory is described in fewer dimensions?

sources.title: Towards a Swampland Global Symmetry Conjecture using weak gravity

evidence.text: How accurately can a low-energy particle number be conserved in quantum gravity? The paper seeks a quantitative operator bound for approximate global symmetries inherited from a massive U(1) gauge theory.

sources.title: Comment on "Braneworld Effective Field Theories -- Holography, Consistency and Conformal Effects"

evidence.text: Can quantum gravity admit a low-energy braneworld EFT containing pure 4D fields on δ-like branes, or must every such field arise from a bulk zero-mode? The paper tests three proposed obstructions rather than constructing a complete UV theory.

sources.title: The Swampland Conjectures: A Bridge from Quantum Gravity to Particle Physics

evidence.text: Which apparently consistent particle-physics EFTs can admit quantum gravity, and can consistency relate parameters that appear independent in an EFT?

sources.title: IR/UV mixing, towers of species and swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Does quantum gravity constrain the independent choice of EFT infrared and ultraviolet cutoffs, and which mass scale characterizes the resulting light spectrum when several towers have different gaps and degeneracies?

sources.title: The Quantum Gravity Scale and the Swampland

evidence.text: What scale controls the breakdown of semiclassical Einstein gravity, and how do its moduli dependence, emergent kinetic terms and infinite-distance behavior constrain gravitational effective theories?

sources.title: Hitchhiker's Guide to the Swampland: The Cosmologist's Handbook to the String‐Theoretical Swampland Programme

evidence.text: Which proposed quantum-gravity consistency constraints restrict cosmological EFTs, especially models of inflation, dark energy, dark matter and black holes, and how strong is their supporting evidence?

sources.title: Phenomenology of low quantum gravity scale models

evidence.text: How can quantum gravity lie far below the four-dimensional Planck scale while accommodating gauge unification, supersymmetry breaking and phenomenology, and which fundamental scales appear motivated?

sources.title: Scales of gravity

evidence.text: Can the quantum-gravity scale M* lie far below the particle-theory cutoff MSM, potentially near 10^(−3) eV, while observed gravity stays weak and an exponentially large tower of bulk states remains compatible with the observations considered?

sources.title: Infinite distance and zero gauge coupling in 5D supergravity

evidence.text: Does the distance–weak-coupling equivalence survive without a nonnegative cubic cone basis? The source leaves this open and reports no counterexamples after relaxing positivity.

sources.title: Black Holes and Large N Species Solution to the Hierarchy Problem

evidence.text: Couple a test string to the Stückelberg field strength through a boundary term and compare linked and unlinked histories. Their phase difference detects global hair despite vanishing local classical fields.

sources.title: Gravity Cutoff in Theories with Large Discrete Symmetries

evidence.text: Matter-spectrum examples test how many particles and species are needed to reproduce an arbitrary discrete charge. Highly charged states can invalidate the single-field discharge argument, while a genuinely large species count can supply an independent reason for a low cutoff.

sources.title: Axion Experiments to Algebraic Geometry: Testing Quantum Gravity via the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Translate weak-gravity bounds into instanton-action constraints, CFT charge/dimension conditions, and wrapped-brane requirements on effective curve classes. These are sketches of applications rather than reproduced derivations.

sources.title: Constraining Neutrino Masses, the Cosmological Constant and BSM Physics from the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Substitute the assumed neutrino mass formula into the eigenmass cap while holding the Yukawa, vacuum energy and specified extra spectrum fixed.

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Remnants from the String Landscape

evidence.text: Solve section-degree constraints without denominator coordinates, extract minimal divisor factors, and identify the candidate fiber. Check monodromy and matter separately before concluding non-Higgsability.

sources.title: Emergence of Weak Coupling at Large Distance in Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Expand about a fixed background, normalize the scalar kinetic term, estimate each state’s propagator correction, and sum states below the probing energy. Solve λ_φ≈1 to estimate strong coupling. The operation retains spectral thresholds but discards numerical factors and detailed loop functions.

sources.title: Lectures on the Swampland Program in String Compactifications

evidence.text: Which states can exactly saturate a quantum-gravitational mass–charge bound?

sources.title: Swampland, Gradient Flow and Infinite Distance

evidence.text: Which limits of effective gravitational theories require additional quantum states, and can geometric evolution of the background identify those limits without first specifying an internal compactification?

sources.title: A Conjecture on the Minimal Size of Bound States

evidence.text: Can attractive interactions produce stable bound states parametrically smaller than the collapse radius of free gravitational boson stars, and does a minimum size persist after gravity decouples?

sources.title: The Weak Gravity Conjecture and Scalar Fields

evidence.text: Can the absence of stable gravitationally bound towers provide a physical principle behind force inequalities in quantum gravity?

sources.title: The Convex Hull Swampland Distance Conjecture and Bounds on Non-geodesics

evidence.text: What limits the distance traversable by adiabatically varying scalar expectation values in an EFT coupled to quantum gravity?

sources.title: The Weak Gravity Conjecture and Scalar Fields

evidence.text: Does a massless force inequality retain quantum-gravity significance after a repulsive gauge field or attractive scalar acquires a small mass?

sources.title: Tensionless Strings and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Which conjectured quantum-gravity constraints can be tested by a controlled compactification limit with a weak gauge interaction and finite gravitational coupling?

sources.title: Quantum Fine-Tuning in Stringy Quintessence Models

evidence.text: The quantum examples ask whether Planck-suppressed matter couplings preserve a classical relation between potential height and slope. Canonical matter kinetic terms provide the baseline against which conformal kinetic couplings are compared.

sources.title: The dark dimension and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can the small observed vacuum-energy density identify an asymptotic quantum-gravity regime and thereby correlate infrared particle scales, extra-dimensional geometry, and the ultraviolet cutoff?

sources.title: The UV fate of anomalous U(1)s and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a massive Abelian vector remain parametrically lighter than the completion of its anomalous infrared spectrum? The paper distinguishes the cancelling-fermion threshold, the further perturbative cutoff, and the quantum gravity scale.

sources.title: The Weak Gravity Conjecture and Scalar Fields

evidence.text: How should a quantum-gravity constraint compare gauge repulsion, gravitational attraction, and scalar forces when scalar geometry and gauge kinetic functions are arbitrary?

sources.title: A Weak gravity conjecture for scalar field theories

evidence.text: Does consistency with quantum gravity impose a parametric upper bound on gravitational strength relative to scalar interactions, detectable through the survival of solitons and their scattering states?

sources.title: Continuum effective field theories, gravity, and holography

evidence.text: When can an EFT with a free or nearly-free continuum consistently include gravity, and how do holographic gapped-continuum realizations modify the Newtonian potential and the brane Friedmann equation?

sources.title: Phenomenological Consequences of the Refined Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Can a proposed quantum-gravity restriction on scalar-potential slopes or negative curvature produce useful low-energy constraints? The paper uses particle potentials and inflationary observations to test the allowed sizes of the conjecture coefficients c and c′.

sources.title: Revisiting the scalar weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Can requiring scalar interactions to dominate gravity restrict scalar effective theories compatible with quantum gravity? The paper explores process-dependent consequences without deriving a general quantum-gravity law.

sources.title: The swampland at large number of space-time dimensions

evidence.text: Can the large-D limit of an apparently consistent gravity effective theory belong to quantum gravity? The paper asks whether known conjectures remain restrictive and whether dimension-dependent tower masses suggest additional restrictions.

sources.title: Snowmass White Paper: Implications of Quantum Gravity for Particle Physics

evidence.text: Review how quantum-gravity consistency conditions constrain low-energy EFT and might inform strong CP, the weak scale, new gauge interactions and dark energy. The white paper explicitly does not guarantee that gravitational considerations solve these problems.

sources.title: Super-Planckian Spatial Field Variations and Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Can quantum-gravity consistency of super-Planckian spatial scalar variations constrain a field-dependent U(1) coupling to decrease exponentially, and determine how quickly that behavior begins beyond the Planck scale?

sources.title: The String landscape and the swampland

evidence.text: Which apparently consistent low-energy theories can occur in a consistent quantum theory of gravity? The paper asks whether universal restrictions on string constructions constrain infrared physics despite the large diversity of known vacua.

sources.title: Quantum (in)stability of maximally symmetric space-times

evidence.text: How do quantum CFT4 effects modify gravitational fluctuation spectra and linear stability around Minkowski, de Sitter and anti-de Sitter backgrounds, and which apparent instabilities fall within gravitational EFT?

sources.title: Sharp boundaries for the swampland

evidence.text: Can the same quantitative consistency program handle general external states, loop discontinuities, infrared-safe four-dimensional scattering, and curved backgrounds? A separate issue is whether the spectra suggested by extremal functionals are realized by physical gravitational theories.

sources.title: Lectures on the Swampland Program in String Compactifications

evidence.text: Could restrictions on EFT parameter space from quantum gravity change naturalness reasoning for the cosmological constant and electroweak hierarchy? The authors suggest UV/IR mixing as a possible connection, motivated by low-energy gravity and weak gauge coupling.

sources.title: Emergence of Weak Coupling at Large Distance in Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: What restrictions does quantum gravity impose on continuous parameters and asymptotic scalar-field geometry? The imported conjectures connect scalar expectation values, infinite moduli-space diameter, and towers becoming exponentially light with geodesic distance.

evidence.text: Can a covariant, background-independent holographic principle identify screens storing the information of general spacetimes, and what do their geometry and changing area imply for possible holographic theories?

sources.title: Linking topological quantum field theory and nonperturbative quantum gravity

evidence.text: Connection and loop representations, spin-network bases, and quantum-spin-network/trinion descriptions imported from conformal field theory. An alternative route solves the surface Gauss constraint using puncture coadjoint orbits before quantization.

sources.title: The World as a hologram

evidence.text: Light-front Hamiltonian reasoning and a renormalization-group analogy treat longitudinal boosts as momentum rescalings. Small-p− divergences motivate a cutoff and a search for boost-invariant fixed points.

sources.title: Holography in general space-times

evidence.text: Slice spacetime into a one-parameter family of null hypersurfaces and project each slice to screens. For spherical examples, Penrose diagrams and apparent horizons determine projection directions and generate screen-hypersurfaces, whose causal character may vary.

sources.title: Linking topological quantum field theory and nonperturbative quantum gravity

evidence.text: CDJ and self-dual variational formulations with a Chern–Simons boundary term; Hamiltonian constraint analysis; ribbon and lattice regularization of boundary second-class constraints to define Dirac brackets.

sources.title: The World as a hologram

evidence.text: Geometric arguments employ null-congruence focusing for screen densities, semiclassical black-hole formation in collisions, and light-cone intersections with a stretched horizon for causal spreading bounds.

sources.title: Holography in general space-times

evidence.text: Use causal containment and the second law to motivate spacelike projection. For evaporation, use null focusing and Raychaudhuri-based reasoning to suggest how infalling density profiles could affect horizon motion and outgoing radiation.

evidence.text: How can causal-diamond entropy, overlap consistency, and black-hole statistical mechanics define holographic quantum systems whose hydrodynamics reproduce spacetime and support an inflationary cosmology with localized excitations?

sources.title: Holographic phenomenology via overlapping degrees of freedom

evidence.text: Can overlapping field-mode algebras reconcile approximately local quantum fields with holographic degree counting, and produce observable consequences for cosmic neutrino propagation?

sources.title: The Holographic bound in anti-de Sitter space

evidence.text: How does AdS/CFT implement the holographic information bound, beyond identifying a gravitational bulk theory with a boundary theory, when both boundary area and boundary entropy are initially infinite?

sources.title: Holographic Inflation Revised

evidence.text: Can Holographic Space-Time provide an inflationary cosmology with long-lived localized excitations, explain its low-entropy initial conditions, and connect primordial fluctuations and reheating to a dilute black-hole gas?

sources.title: Brane gases in the early universe: Thermodynamics and cosmology

evidence.text: Can early-universe M2-brane thermodynamics, creation and annihilation leave winding relics that select three decompactifying dimensions, when initial states are sampled statistically and constrained by holography?

sources.title: One-loop effect of null-like cosmology's holographic dual super-Yang-Mills

evidence.text: Does the holographic SYM dual of a null-like cosmology retain boson–fermion cancellation of one-loop vacuum energy for arbitrary null-dependent BPS scalar profiles, and what does this indicate about particle production, ultraviolet behavior and the bulk singularity?

sources.title: Holographic Inflation Revised

evidence.text: Impose unitary equivalence of density matrices on overlapping causal diamonds. Copy appropriate inside-horizon dynamics into another trajectory's outside factor, then match coarse-grained quantum dynamics to FRW hydrodynamics.

sources.title: Brane gases in the early universe: Thermodynamics and cosmology

evidence.text: A semiclassical microcanonical ensemble imposes Hgravity+Ematter=0. Integrating the energy constraint gives a phase-space weight proportional to V^d exp(Smatter); entropy maximization at fixed geometry determines equilibrium temperature and total membrane area.

sources.title: One-loop effect of null-like cosmology's holographic dual super-Yang-Mills

evidence.text: Use background-field gauge, include Faddeev–Popov ghosts, expand to quadratic order, and successively perform Gaussian integrations over gauge and scalar fluctuations.

sources.title: Holographic Inflation Revised

evidence.text: Estimate fluctuations using finite-entropy thermodynamics and reheating using semiclassical black-hole evaporation, matter-era dilution and the energy-density–temperature relation. These are model calculations rather than independently checked derivations here.

sources.title: Holographic Inflation Revised

evidence.text: Construct Hamiltonians as traces of finite-order polynomials in fermion bilinears M. Count vanishing off-diagonal elements as localization constraints and relate entropy deficits to localized energy.

sources.title: Brane gases in the early universe: Thermodynamics and cosmology

evidence.text: A covariant entropy-bound analysis is applied to an isotropic square torus. For spheres inside the apparent horizon dAH=1/λ̇, sV≤A/(4G) gives R≤d/(4Gs), which is translated into a restriction on torus size.

sources.title: Fine-tuning and the Second Law of Thermodynamics from the perspective of de Sitter quantum gravity

evidence.text: Can quantum gravity and holography reframe Higgs-mass and cosmological-constant fine-tuning by making bulk IR parameters fundamental, while allowing a past-to-future Second Law to emerge from future de Sitter boundary conditions?

sources.title: Holography for the very early Universe and the classic puzzles of Hot Big Bang cosmology

evidence.text: Can a non-geometric holographic early universe address the smoothness/horizon, flatness, and relic problems through properties of the dual QFT's RG flow, and offer an account of the arrow of time?
